subject: Publishable privacy blurbs & subprocessor map for upcoming demo
body:
From: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — publishable privacy blurbs for demo

Marcus — thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Our pre-demo checklist calls for a short, consumer-friendly privacy paragraph and a high-level subprocessor list we can show during an executive demo (not the full DPA). Can you share: 1) one-or-two sentence publishable blurbs we can put on a slide, 2) a simple subprocessor map (country + purpose) scoped to Hosted API only, and 3) a one-liner about cross-border transfers / safeguards we can read aloud?

Ideally we need these by EOD Wednesday so the Sales deck gets finalized. Appreciate it —
Sofia
Sofia Ramos
Senior Program Manager, Acme Corp

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — publishable privacy blurbs for demo

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear ask. Attached are two deliverables: a short blurb doc with three alternative phrasings (consumer, sales, and legal-lite) and a CSV subprocessor map filtered to Hosted API. Below are the three candidate blurbs and a single-line transfer script you can read during the demo. Pick the tone you want and we can lock it down.

Publishable blurbs (pick one):
1) Consumer (plain): "Redwood Inference processes customer requests to generate responses. We limit data retention, use industry-standard security controls, and only share data with subprocessors to deliver and maintain the service."
2) Sales-friendly: "Redwood runs inference in secure environments, minimizes data retention, and partners with a small set of subprocessors for hosting and telemetry — everything required to keep your service fast and reliable."
3) Legal-lite: "Redwood acts as a processor for customer inputs processed via the Hosted API. Data handling is governed by our DPA; subprocessors are engaged only to provide hosting, telemetry, and monitoring services under contractual safeguards."

Transfer line (one-liner):
"We route requests through cloud regions and use standard contractual safeguards plus encryption in transit and at rest to protect cross-border transfers."

Please note: the attached subprocessor CSV lists company, country, and purpose (hosting/CDN/logging/monitoring). We redacted vendor contract IDs — happy to provide if procurement needs a copy.

Attachments: redwood_publishable_privacy_blurbs_v1.docx (3 phrases + notes), subprocessor_map_acme_slice.csv (filtered)

Marcus Lin
Senior Product Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

--

Great start, Marcus. A couple of small edits to help Sales read naturally on slides: shorten the consumer blurb and avoid the word "processes" (it reads legal). Suggest: "Redwood powers features while minimizing data retention, using encryption and trusted subprocessors only as needed."

Also, add a 1-sentence footnote for the slide: "Full DPA available upon request; this summary is for demo only."

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Marketing
Redwood Inference

One quick ask from Sales ops: can we include a short residency note when the customer asks about data locality? Proposed inline: "Customers may select preferred regions for Hosted API; data can be pinned to cloud regions where available."

Also, procurement sometimes wants a DocuSign shortcut — I added a DocuSign link in the related_links; procurement@acme-corp.com, if you prefer a signed DPA excerpt we can route that for review.

Thanks all — Sofia, final answer below (ready-to-drop onto a slide). If you want the slightly more formal legal-lite line, say so and we'll swap.

Final publishable blurb (sales tone — single line):
"Redwood runs inference in secure cloud regions, minimizes retention by default, and uses a limited set of subprocessors to provide hosting and monitoring."

Residency note (short):
"Customers can select preferred cloud regions for Hosted API where available to meet data locality needs."

Transfer line (spoken):
"We use encryption plus contractual safeguards for cross-border transfers and can provide the DPA on request."

I attached the docx + CSV. Let me know if procurement needs vendor contracts redacted differently.

-Marcus
